_doc: How a person judges a deed people weigh by their own nature (PlayerEvents opts.morals; docs/WORLD_SCHEMA.md §16). Taverns.judge(who, morals) reads the person's own data: a main NPC's soul (resources/npc_personalities: core_values, dislikes, interests, Big Five, flags, romance fields), world.json role, and the relationship with the player; a generic's archetype, its rolled Voice variant and rolled Big Five. Each rule lists conditions that must ALL hold; a word list matches when any word is found (lower case, substring) in any entry of that field. Within a group only the strongest rule (largest |weight|) counts; groups add up and the sum is clamped to range. A `tone` rule weighs nothing: it only gives its `feels` line in place of the strongest rule's. `courting` beats everything: someone courting the player is hurt, whatever else they think. Children are never asked (they weigh 0 and their knowledge carries no reaction). `reason` is for people reading the tables (debug, tests); `feels` is the person's own view, in the first person, put beside what they know of the deed in their prompt. Nothing here is ever explicit.

default.reason: nothing in their nature cares what a stranger does behind a closed door
default.feels: What a stranger does behind a closed door is their own business, not mine.

courting._doc: A main NPC who could love the player (is_romantic_available, an orientation not in never) and either has the romance (one of flags set, or their soul's romance thresholds met) weighs styles[relationship_style]; one only growing fond (affection >= affection_share x their own romance_affection_threshold) weighs that times budding_scale
courting.reason: they are courting the player, and it hurts
courting.feels: It hurts more than I will say, after what has passed between us.

rules.feels: It sits ill with me. That is no way to live before the Dawn, and I think the less of them for it.
It sits ill with me. That is no way to live before the Dawn, and I think the less of them for it.
It is not how the Dawn would have us live. I will pray for them, but I think the less of them.
It is a shameful thing, and I will say so if they ask me. I will pray for them.

rules.reason: mercy among their values: they disapprove without casting anyone out
rules.feels: It sits ill with me, before the Dawn. But I have nursed worse sinners than that, and I will not turn them from my door.

rules.reason: they keep to propriety and standing
rules.feels: It is not a thing a decent person is seen doing, and I mark it.
I have no time for that sort of carrying on, and I think the less of them for it.

rules.reason: strait-laced: dutiful and set in their ways
rules.feels: Not the sort of thing I hold with.

rules.reason: prim, and disapproving of anyone who is not
rules.feels: Well. I know what I think of that, and so will they.

rules.reason: they have an eye for others themselves: not one to talk
rules.feels: I am hardly one to talk.
Good luck to them. A stranger who likes their comforts is easier company.

rules.reason: coin spent is coin earned, to them
rules.feels: Coin spent is coin moving, and that is no shame to anyone.

rules.reason: they keep the house whose back rooms it is: good custom
rules.feels: Good custom for the house. They paid and kept the house's terms.

rules.reason: it is their own living, and the stranger paid fair
rules.feels: They paid fair and minded the house's terms. What passes behind the door stays there.
